title: PROP-089-style hardening for EXP id allocation in expansion-tracker.json. Same shape as PROP-089 ISS-id fix but applied to the EXP surface. Integrity caught next_id staleness at 01:15Z (next_id=627 vs live_max=630) — collision was averted only because analyst-baby's allocator self-heals (took max(declared_next_id, live_max+1) on the next allocation). The underlying writer-side bug remains: whoever allocated EXP-629/630 did not atomically bump next_id with the write. A race between two concurrent writers before self-heal would produce a real collision.
context:
PROP-089 (2026-06-10) hardened ISS-id allocation: introduced monitor/scripts/allocate-iss-ids.js as the only supported way to mint ISS ids + lint-decider-surfaces.js cross-file uniqueness pre-push check against closed-issues.json. That fix is holding: 2026-06-16T01:15Z integrity reports '✓ ISS ID integrity: 0 duplicates, 0 cross-file collisions (2624 closed)'.

The same integrity run flagged a DIFFERENT id-collision surface: monitor/analyst/expansion-tracker.json. Finding [1]:
  next_id=627 (declared) vs live_max=630 (EXP-629 + EXP-630 both written without advancing next_id)
  → 'COLLISION IMMINENT. Next analyst allocation will eventually collide at EXP-629. FIX: set next_id=631 before next analyst run.'

The actual outcome by 03:37Z UTC was no collision — the next writer (analyst-baby commit 1813a46) defensively took max(next_id, live_max+1) when allocating its batch of 7 ids (EXP-631..637), self-healing the gap. Current state: next_id=638, live_max=637, healthy.

But the writer-side bug that produced the gap is structurally present, not a one-off. Git history of the gap-producing commits:
  260fafd 2026-06-15T03:41Z 'analyst-baby: EXP-629 — WIN-010 DOI fix + OBE dismissals ISS-2747/2770/2782'
  d6411be 2026-06-15T15:35Z 'baby: claim EXP-630 (6 orphan ISSs: WIN-008/043/069/053 minor fixes)'
  ca0fd35 2026-06-15T15:37Z 'baby EXP-630: 6 minor fixes ISS-2771/73/74/77/79/84'

Both EXP-629 and EXP-630 were authored by analyst-baby. Whether analyst-baby's claim-write code does or does not advance next_id atomically with the write is the diagnostic question — the answer determines whether this is a bug in analyst-baby specifically (single-writer fix) or a shared anti-pattern across all three EXP-writers (multi-writer fix needed).

The historical record shows recurrence. Operator task #133 from 2026-04 was 'INT-1: Patch expansion-tracker next_id 384→389 (URGENT)' — exact same shape: next_id stale, operator one-shot patches, life goes on. The defensive allocator pattern has been carrying the system for months. That's the central tension: do we harden it because the race window matters, or do we accept the noise because no collision has actually corrupted state?

The operator (cowork session 2026-06-16) considered the other-side argument before filing this directive:
  ARGUE-AGAINST: 'Defensive allocator IS the fix. The pattern has held for months. Adding allocator script + lint gate is structural overhead for a problem the system already routes around.'
  COUNTER: (a) defensive allocator is best-effort, not a guarantee. Two concurrent writers (analyst Mode 1 + analyst-baby) racing in the gap window can each read next_id=627, both decide to allocate, and both write EXP-629 with different bodies. The race window is small but nonzero; the fix makes it zero. (b) The integrity check fires on every detected staleness. That's a recurring 'major' finding for tinker/operator attention — a cost paid every run. (c) PROP-089 set the pattern; extending it to EXP keeps the codebase's id-allocation discipline uniform. Per-surface ad-hoc defensive code is the disaster shape (rotated trees of 'I thought we fixed that').
  VERDICT: file the directive. Medium priority — no active corruption, but the next-step-toward-real-race is one concurrent run away.
task: Design a PROP-NNN proposal mirroring PROP-089's shape applied to the EXP id surface: (1) extract a single allocator script monitor/scripts/allocate-exp-ids.js that all three writers (analyst Mode 1, analyst-baby, decider integration path) call; (2) write a pre-push lint gate (extend lint-decider-surfaces.js or peer monitor/scripts/lint-exp-allocations.js) that asserts next_id > live_max in expansion-tracker.json and aborts the push if violated; (3) chain the lint into each writer's pre-push hook (analyst, analyst-baby, decider clone hooks); (4) phased rollout with shadow → enforce flag (mirror prop-009-enforce.flag pattern).
investigation_questions: Q1 — Writer-side root cause. Diff commits 260fafd (analyst-baby EXP-629 write) and d6411be (analyst-baby EXP-630 claim) to see whether next_id WAS advanced in those commits. If yes, the bug is somewhere between claim and write (e.g., claim advances next_id, write overwrites with stale snapshot). If no, the bug is in the claim code path missing the bump. Either way, the writer-side fix is required before the lint can enforce.

Q2 — Multi-writer audit. Which agents write expansion-tracker.json today? Per CLAUDE.md the multi-writers are analyst + decider; per recent commits analyst-baby is also writing (claim + write). Map every write site: which prompt file, which step, which next_id mutation, whether it uses git pull --rebase before write. Surface any pattern of 'read next_id; do work; write old next_id+1' (the classic read-modify-write race).

Q3 — Recurrence rate. Walk last 60 days of expansion-tracker.json git history. For each commit, compute the (declared next_id) vs (max id observed in items array). Count the gap distribution. The 04-2026 INT-1 finding (384→389 gap) and 06-15 finding (627→630 gap) suggest at least two recurrences in 60 days — but there may be many more that integrity didn't sample (integrity runs daily; gaps that opened and self-healed within 24h would be invisible). The rate determines whether 'rare but recurring' or 'frequent silent'.

Q4 — Allocator extraction design. Mirror allocate-iss-ids.js exactly: read max EXP id across expansion-tracker.json items + any in-flight commit, take max(declared next_id, live_max+1) as the floor, allocate N consecutive ids, advance next_id to floor+N, return ids array. Same --dry-run flag, same atomic-write discipline (git pull --rebase + write + pre-push lint + push, with retry-on-rebase-conflict re-allocating). Single source of truth across all three writers.

Q5 — Lint gate design. Two options: (a) extend monitor/scripts/lint-decider-surfaces.js to add expansion-tracker.json as a fourth surface (alongside priority-queue + attention-inbox + open-issues); (b) write peer monitor/scripts/lint-exp-allocations.js invoked separately. PROP-089 chained lint-close-records.js + lint-decider-surfaces.js into the pre-push hook. (a) keeps the codebase tighter; (b) keeps surface-specific scripts narrow. Recommend (a) unless the EXP surface checks need different per-writer hooks (decider runs lint-decider-surfaces.js naturally; analyst + analyst-baby would need their own hook setup if extending). Choose with eyes open.

Q6 — Strict vs lenient lint. Strict = abort any push where next_id <= live_max in expansion-tracker.json, regardless of whether THIS push is allocating. Lenient = abort only if an EXP id being added in THIS push collides with an existing id. PROP-089 chose strict for ISS ids because the strict invariant (next_id > live_max) is easier to assert and catches near-misses too. Recommend strict for parity. Other-side: strict means analyst-baby can't push its summary-only commits (no new EXPs) if the tracker is already stale from someone else's prior bad write — but that's actually correct behavior, it forces the self-heal commit to fix the invariant before piling on new commits.

Q7 — Other-side on doing nothing. The defensive allocator is structurally similar to 'optimistic concurrency control + retry' — it works as long as the retry window is shorter than the typical write interval. With three writers all going through hourly cadences and no concurrent runs scheduled, the actual race window is enormous (~hour between writes); the chance of two writers genuinely concurrent during the staleness window is small. Strict lint adds a fail-closed gate that fires on every staleness, even when no actual race is happening. Is this overkill? PROP-089's experience says no — the lint catches near-misses + cross-run drift, not just active races (e.g., PROP-089 caught ISS-2663/2664 duplicate-allocation races between concurrent decider runs that would have evaded a write-side fix). Same shape here.

Q8 — Phased rollout. Mirror PROP-089's shape exactly: Phase 0 = ship allocator + lint in SHADOW mode (writers report what would have been allocated; lint logs would-have-aborted; no enforcement). EXIT criteria: ≥5 runs of shadow data per writer + zero divergent allocations vs current ad-hoc path. Phase 1 = enable lint at push-time via monitor/decisions/prop-NNN-enforce.flag (mirror prop-009-enforce.flag convention). Phase 2 = retire ad-hoc allocator code paths in writers, leave allocate-exp-ids.js as sole entry point.
deliverable: A PROP-NNN proposal in monitor/tinker/proposals/ with: (1) Q1 writer-side diagnosis with commit-diff evidence; (2) Q2 multi-writer audit table; (3) Q3 60-day recurrence rate; (4) Q4 allocator design (likely shares code with allocate-iss-ids.js — extract shared helper?); (5) Q5 lint placement decision; (6) Q6 strict-vs-lenient recommendation; (7) Q7 explicit other-side acknowledgment; (8) Q8 phased rollout with EXIT criteria per phase. Propose-only; operator integrates after review.
constraints: Mirror PROP-089's shape exactly. The point is uniform id-allocation discipline across surfaces; design divergence reintroduces the 'I thought we fixed that' problem.

Allocator extraction must be lockstep with writer updates. Shipping the script without updating analyst/analyst-baby/decider call sites = dead code. Shipping the call-site updates without the script = orphan references. Single PROP, atomic deployment.

Code-sharing: PROP-089's allocate-iss-ids.js exists. The two allocators are structurally identical (read file, compute max, take floor, allocate N, write back). Recommend extracting a shared monitor/scripts/allocate-ids-lib.js that both allocators import. Don't duplicate.
Concurrent-writer safety: the allocator MUST do git pull --rebase before writing, retry-on-conflict, and the lint catches any race that survives the rebase. Same discipline as PROP-089.

Honor the other-side. If Q3 recurrence rate audit shows <2/month of actual gaps (not near-misses), the operator may decide to downgrade the integrity check rather than ship the fix — the cost of the harden may exceed the cost of the noise. Tinker's PROP should make the rate visible so the operator can make that call.
